name: Question 11
worked_solution:
Our function can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt{\frac{{({x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8)}^{2}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{{({x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8)}^{2}}}{\sqrt{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8}{(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{1/2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the quotient and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8}{(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{1/2}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8)-\operatorname{ln}⁡((\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{1/2}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =\frac{1}{{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8}\cdot (4{x}^{3}+4x)-\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{4{x}^{3}+4x}{{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8}+\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}{2} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{8{x}^{3}+8x}{{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8}+\operatorname{tan}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{y}{2}(\frac{8{x}^{3}+8x}{{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8}+\operatorname{tan}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=\sqrt{\frac{{({x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8)}^{2}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\sqrt{\frac{{({x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8)}^{2}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}\cdot \frac{1}{2}(\frac{8{x}^{3}+8x}{{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8}+\operatorname{tan}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{|{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8|}{2\sqrt{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}(\frac{8{x}^{3}+8x}{{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8}+\operatorname{tan}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8>0\text{ }∀x\in R$, so $|{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8|={x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8$ and we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8}{2\sqrt{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}(\frac{8{x}^{3}+8x}{{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8}+\operatorname{tan}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}[\frac{8{x}^{3}+8x}{{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8}\cdot ({x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8)+\operatorname{tan}⁡x({x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8)] \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}(8{x}^{3}+8x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x({x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+8))\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11

Given that y=(x4+2x2+8)2cos⁡x, find y′.
y′=12cos⁡x(
8x3+8x
+tan⁡x(x4+2x2+8))

EXPLANATION

Our function can be written as

y=(x4+2x2+8)2cos⁡x=(x4+2x2+8)2cos⁡x=x4+2x2+8(cos⁡x)1/2.

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the quotient and power rules for logarithms:

ln⁡y=ln⁡(x4+2x2+8(cos⁡x)1/2)ln⁡y=ln⁡(x4+2x2+8)−ln⁡((cos⁡x)1/2)ln⁡y=ln⁡(x4+2x2+8)−12ln⁡(cos⁡x)

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to x:

ddx(ln⁡y)=ddx(ln⁡(x4+2x2+8)−12ln⁡(cos⁡x))1y⋅y′=1x4+2x2+8⋅(4x3+4x)−12⋅1cos⁡x⋅(−sin⁡x)y′y=4x3+4xx4+2x2+8+tan⁡x2y′y=12(8x3+8xx4+2x2+8+tan⁡x)

Now, we solve for y′:

y′=y2(8x3+8xx4+2x2+8+tan⁡x)

Finally, we substitute y=(x4+2x2+8)2cos⁡x:

y′=(x4+2x2+8)2cos⁡x⋅12(8x3+8xx4+2x2+8+tan⁡x)=|x4+2x2+8|2cos⁡x(8x3+8xx4+2x2+8+tan⁡x)

Since x4+2x2+8>0 ∀x∈R, so |x4+2x2+8|=x4+2x2+8 and we have:

y′=x4+2x2+82cos⁡x(8x3+8xx4+2x2+8+tan⁡x)=12cos⁡x[8x3+8xx4+2x2+8⋅(x4+2x2+8)+tan⁡x(x4+2x2+8)]=12cos⁡x(8x3+8x+tan⁡x(x4+2x2+8))
